portInfo.description: Cannes is more than a film-festival façade. Le Suquet rises above the old harbour, while the Croisette runs along a much flatter seafront past the Palais. This geography makes a compact self-guided day possible, but the tender crossing is still part of the time budget. An old tourism article is useful for the street pattern, not proof that every market, museum name or business listed in 2012 is unchanged.

climate.rainySeason: Year-round with higher precipitation in autumn

politics.visaRequirements: Entry and visa rules depend on nationality. Many visitors use Schengen short-stay rules, but requirements change—confirm with official government sources and your cruise line before travel.
politics.entryRequirements: Carry a valid passport (or a national ID where your cruise line and destination authorities accept it). Cruise transit formalities can differ from a normal airport entry—follow your ship’s document list.

gettingThere.fromTerminal: Vieux-Port — Cruise Shuttles landing — Quai du Large at the Quai des Îles junction,Vieux-Port,Cannes
gettingThere.distanceToCity: The 2026 IGY map places Cruise Shuttles at the Quai du Large/Quai des Îles junction area, south of the yacht basins; it separately labels the Lérins ticket office/pier nearer Quai Laubeuf. Allow 45 minutes for outward tender/queue and 20–30 minutes on foot toward Le Suquet or the Palais, depending on the actual exit through works. A local ferry to the islands is an ADDITIONAL boat transfer, not the ship’s tender. Taxi/train trips to Nice or Monaco are not short extensions of this central walking route.
gettingThere.publicTransport: Confirm local transport options with the ship on your call date.

thingsToDo.intro: Pick one neighbourhood or excursion scale and keep time for the gangway queue on the way back.
topThings: Le Suquet, Le Suquet hill via the old-town lanes, Cannes: Climb to the historic quarter for views over harbour and bay. Allow about 90 minutes (editorial estimate). Steep lanes and steps; choose the waterfront instead if needed.

La Croisette, Boulevard de la Croisette at the Palais, Cannes: A flat seafront stretch with the city’s best-known hotel and cinema setting. Allow about 60 minutes (editorial estimate). Public beach access and individual venues have separate rules.

Palais des Festivals exterior and cinema handprints, Palais des Festivals/Esplanade Pompidou, Cannes: Look for the cinema landmarks without assuming interior admission. Allow about 40 minutes (editorial estimate). Red-carpet/event areas can be controlled; no current tour is guaranteed.

Forville market area — redevelopment-aware visit, Marché Forville and signed temporary trading sites, Cannes: A current local-food stop only after checking the municipality’s split-site directions. Allow about 45 minutes (editorial estimate). Do not promise normal access to the whole hall or the future roof garden.

Rue Meynadier, Rue Meynadier, Cannes: Use the pedestrian food-shopping street as a lower-town link rather than another vehicle transfer. Allow about 40 minutes (editorial estimate). Individual shops and opening times are not verified.
